title: 07. Advanced & Agentic RAG: What is MCP and Why Does It Exist?
summary: Imagine it is the year 2010. You have a laptop, a phone, a camera, and a pair of headphones.
objectives: ① Real-World Analogy — The USB-C Story
⑤ The Real-World Example — Claude Reading a File

sections.title: ① Real-World Analogy — The USB-C Story
sections.body:
Imagine it is the year 2010. You have a laptop, a phone, a camera, and a pair of headphones. Every single device has a **different charger**. Your phone uses micro-USB, your camera uses mini-USB, your laptop has a proprietary connector, and your headphones have their own weird plug. Every time you travel, you need to carry 4 different cables.

Then USB-C was invented. **One connector. Every device. Every manufacturer. Everywhere.**

That is exactly what MCP is — but for AI agents and the tools they use.

Before MCP existed, every AI company built their own way of giving tools to their AI agent. OpenAI had one way. Anthropic had another. LangChain had yet another. If you built a file-reading tool for Claude, it wouldn't work with ChatGPT without rewriting it completely. Every connection was a custom cable.

**MCP is the USB-C for AI tools.** Build your tool once. Every agent that supports MCP can use it immediately.

sections.title: ② Plain English Explanation
sections.body:
MCP stands for **Model Context Protocol**. It was created by Anthropic in 2024 and is now an open standard.

Here is what it does in plain English:

- It defines a **standard language** that AI agents and tools use to talk to each other
- It works like a **contract**: "If you speak MCP, I will understand you, no matter who built you"
- It separates the **AI brain** (Claude, GPT, Gemini) from the **tools** (file reader, calculator, database)
- This means you can build a tool **once** and use it with **any MCP-compatible AI agent**

Think of it like a common spoken language. If everyone in a room speaks English, they can all understand each other — even if they are from different countries.

sections.title: ③ Why Does This Matter?
sections.body:
**The problem MCP solves:** Before MCP, every AI framework had its own tool format. A tool written for LangChain would not work in OpenAI's agent system without rewriting. This was wasteful and frustrating.

**What MCP gives you:** Write your tool once → plug it into Claude, GPT, Gemini, LangChain, LangGraph, or any other MCP-compatible system. Zero rewriting.

**Why Veera should care:** When you finish this course, you will build tools that work everywhere — not just in one framework. Your skills become universally applicable.

sections.title: ④ Step-by-Step Technical Explanation
sections.body:
Let us understand MCP's architecture. There are **four key players** in every MCP interaction:

### The Four Players

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PLAYER 1: HOST                                     │
│  The application the user is running                │
│  Examples: Claude Desktop, VS Code with Copilot,   │
│            your own Python application              │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PLAYER 2: CLIENT                                   │
│  Lives inside the Host                              │
│  Responsible for connecting to MCP servers          │
│  The "phone" that dials out to tool servers         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PLAYER 3: SERVER                                   │
│  The program YOU build                              │
│  Exposes tools, resources, and prompts              │
│  Waits for the client to call it                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  PLAYER 4: TRANSPORT                                │
│  The "road" between client and server               │
│  Can be stdio (local) or HTTP (network)             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### How They Connect — Step by Step

```
Step 1: User opens Claude Desktop (HOST starts)
Step 2: Claude Desktop starts an MCP CLIENT inside itself
Step 3: The CLIENT launches your MCP SERVER as a subprocess
Step 4: They shake hands — this is called "initialization"
Step 5: Claude (the AI) decides it needs to read a file
Step 6: CLIENT sends a "call this tool" message to SERVER
Step 7: SERVER runs your code and sends back the result
Step 8: Claude receives the result and continues its response
```

sections.title: ⑤ The Real-World Example — Claude Reading a File
sections.body:
Let us make this very concrete. Imagine Claude Desktop is open on your computer and you say:

> "Hey Claude, what is in my `/home/veera/notes.txt` file?"

Here is what happens behind the scenes:

```
YOU (user) ──────────► CLAUDE DESKTOP (Host)
                              │
                              │ "I need a file reading tool"
                              ▼
                         MCP CLIENT
                              │
                              │ "Hey File Server, read /home/veera/notes.txt"
                              ▼
                     YOUR MCP SERVER
                     (file_server.py)
                              │
                              │ Opens file, reads content
                              │
                              │ Returns: "Meeting at 3pm, buy milk"
                              ▼
                         MCP CLIENT
                              │
                              │ Hands result back to Claude
                              ▼
                         CLAUDE (AI)
                              │
                              │ "Your notes say: Meeting at 3pm, buy milk"
                              ▼
                           YOU ◄─────────────────────────────────────────
```

**You, as the developer, only write the `file_server.py` part.** MCP handles everything else.

sections.title: ⑥ What MCP Is NOT
sections.body:
This is important. Beginners often confuse MCP with other things:

```
MCP is NOT a database        ← it does not store your data
MCP is NOT an API framework  ← it is not like Flask or FastAPI
MCP is NOT a library         ← it is a protocol (a set of rules)
MCP is NOT only for Claude   ← any AI agent can use it
MCP is NOT complicated       ← you will build one today by Lesson 7!
```

sections.title: ⑦ Quick Recap — What Did We Just Learn?
sections.body:
- ✅ MCP = USB-C for AI tools (one standard, every agent)
- ✅ Four players: Host, Client, Server, Transport
- ✅ YOU build the Server — everything else is handled for you
- ✅ Build a tool once → works with Claude, GPT, Gemini, LangChain, etc.
- ✅ MCP is a protocol (a set of rules), not a library or database
